items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: then I got the job with Willie Pajeaud, on El Alamo, at Burgundy and Canal [streets].

ctx.x: Where did you work? Which store?

Store was Senais [? (spelling)] and Soloman. There’s this church . . . school on the corner, on the side of it, on Orleans and . . . can’t think of that street. I worked there. I was a delivery boy. Saw some hell of a sights back then. Worked there ’til I started playing full time, and then I got the job with Willie Pajeaud, on El Alamo, at Burgundy and Canal [streets]. Upstairs over the Woolworth, there was a hall up there, El Alamo. It was a dime a dance. [recording engineer:] We need to stop so I can change…
You were telling me that you joined Willie Pajeaud’s band, and you played at a place on Canal Street above where the Woolworth’s is.

items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: I worked with gang of bands, dancing schools and different bands. You know, Willie Pajo's band.

ctx.x: Who did Lloyd Arthur Dog play with?

He played with the Arnold Brass Band. They played first clarinet. He died young with a social disease. My great-aunt term. He was a shy boy. He was a basketball sergeant. Some sportswoman enticed him and got in a corral and contacted his disease. And they wouldn't tell the old folks that he was sick. And somehow they detected that he had this trouble. And when they found out about it and rushed him to the hospital, it was too late. So he died of this sickness. And this is just a lot on the planet. So Michael Paul…
Back to Florida for a minute. What were the bands like in Florida other than the band you were with?
